therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: antipsychotic symptom suppression and medication adherence improvement
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with chronic psychotic disorders (schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder) in Tanzania with medication nonadherence
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change in TRQ adherence score from baseline to 6 months; count of participants receiving all LAI injections

results.effect_size: TRQ Week adherence: -57% change; TRQ Month adherence: -23% change; 18/22 participants received all LAI injections
safety_signals: 1 serious adverse event: substance use relapse and hospitalization (1/19 participants)
Extrapyramidal symptoms (parkinsonism, dystonia, dyskinesia, akathisia) were minimal and stable or improved over 25 weeks

dose_info.dose: Haloperidol decanoate mean ~68 mg (SD 21.1, range 50-100 mg) per monthly injection
dose_info.schedule: Monthly intramuscular injection; up to 8 injections over 6 months
dose_info.dose_modifications: Dose changes permitted based on clinical status; oral tolerance test of up to 14 days oral haloperidol 2-5 mg once or twice daily prior to LAI initiation for non-haloperidol patients

modulation_entries.hypothesis: CAE behavioral intervention improves medication adherence, thereby ensuring consistent delivery and sustained biological effect of haloperidol decanoate on dopamine receptor antagonism and symptom suppression
modulation_entries.citation: CAE will be delivered in approximately 8 sessions by a nurse interventionist, ideally at the same time that the long-acting injectable (LAI) is administered. CAE targets key areas relevant to adherence in chronic psychotic disorders (CPD): 1.) inadequate understanding of mental disorder, 2.) lack of adequate medication-taking routines, 3.) poor communication with care providers and 4.) substance use which interferes with adherence and recovery.
